newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News Ltd exec chairman Cowley steps down.
newsitem.headline: News Ltd exec chairman Cowley steps down.

text.p: News Corp Ltd chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch said on Tuesday that Ken Cowley had decided to retire as executive chairman of News Corp's Australian unit, News Ltd.
Murdoch said his son, Lachlan Murdoch, would assume overall responsibility for the Australian operations.
In a statement issued from Los Angeles, Rupert Murdoch said he regretfully accepted Cowley's decision to retire at the end of June.
Cowley, 62, would remain a director of News Corp and continue as chairman of Ansett International and Ansett New Zealand, as well as director of some other listed firms controlled by News Corp.
"As managing director of News Ltd, Mr Lachlan Murdoch will assume overall responsibility for our Australian operations," Murdoch said.

"Mr Cowley has acted as mentor to many executives who have gone onto leadership positions within News Corp. I know that they share my great respect, admiration and gratitude to him, and look forward to continuing to draw upon his expertise," Rupert Murdoch said.
Cowley joined News 33 years ago when he helped Murdoch launch The Australian national newspaper.
He was made managing director of News Ltd in 1980, chairman and chief executive in 1992 and executive chairman in 1996.
Cowley is a member of the News Corp executive management committee which was established in 1995.

Lachlan Murdoch, the eldest of Rupert Murdoch's two sons, was appointed managing director of the Australian operations on September 23 last year and joined the board of the parent company on October 29.

Media analysts have speculated in the last year or so that either Lachlan or his elder sister Elisabeth would eventually take control of the international media firm once their 66-year-old father chose to stand aside.
Elisabeth is now an executive with News Corp affiliate British Sky Broadcasting Plc in London.
